chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he used to say:

One who supplicates for his brothers among the believers and the believing women, and the Muslims and the Muslim women, Allah appoints for him an angel who supplicates for him on behalf of every believer.

key_terms.إِخْوَانِهِ: his brothers (plural of brother, often used for fellow believers)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for supplicating for other believers according to Imam al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, Imam al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) elucidates the mechanism of spiritual reciprocity, where Allah appoints a specific angel to supplicate for the donor on behalf of each believer they prayed for. This narration underscores the communal solidarity (*ta’awun*) in Shia piety, transforming individual supplication into a collective intercessory act that multiplies divine mercy through angelic mediation.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s.) said, “One who supplicates for believers,  the  Almighty  Allah  appoints  an  angel  for  each believer to supplicate for that person.”
